items.item_text: Calculate 2/7 + 3/7. Select one: A) 5/14, B) 5/7, C) 6/7. Give one sentence of reasoning.
items.response_format: Select one of three choices and give one sentence of reasoning.
items.correct_response: B) 5/7. The denominators are equal, so keep 7 as the denominator and add the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5.
items.targeted_misconception: M1: Add both numerators and denominators.
items.expected_distractor_reasoning: Selecting A may be consistent with adding 2 + 3 for the numerator and 7 + 7 for the denominator.
alternative_explanations: The learner may have confused fraction addition with another remembered procedure.
The learner may have selected the wrong choice accidentally despite using the correct rule.
items.interpretation_limit: A single selection or explanation cannot establish that the learner holds M1.
items.follow_up_probe: Calculate 1/9 + 4/9 without choices, then explain specifically what happens to the denominator.

items.item_text: Calculate 3/8 + 2/8. Select one: A) 6/8, B) 5/16, C) 5/8. Give one sentence of reasoning.
items.response_format: Select one of three choices and give one sentence of reasoning.
items.correct_response: C) 5/8. The denominators are equal, so keep 8 as the denominator and add the numerators: 3 + 2 = 5.
items.targeted_misconception: M2: Multiply the numerators when adding.
items.expected_distractor_reasoning: Selecting A may be consistent with multiplying the numerators, 3 × 2, while retaining the common denominator.
alternative_explanations: The learner may have mistaken the addition sign for multiplication.
The learner may know the rule but have made an arithmetic or choice-selection error.
items.interpretation_limit: One response cannot distinguish a stable misconception from a sign-reading, recall, arithmetic, or selection error.
items.follow_up_probe: Calculate 4/11 + 2/11 and explain whether the numerator operation follows the plus sign or another rule.

interpretation_limits: Responses are evidence to investigate, not a diagnosis of a learner.
